Project layout

The files in a command-based project

FileIts jobKeep in mind
Robot.javaCreates RobotContainer and runs the scheduler every loopKeep it mostly empty
RobotContainer.javaCreates subsystems and controllers, and binds them to commandsMost of your setup goes here
Constants.javaGives every number a name, grouped by subsystemNo logic in this file
subsystems/CANDriveSubsystem.javaOwns the motors and offers commandsNothing else touches the motors

Project setup

Creating the project and installing REVLib

1

Open the WPILib command palette

Press Ctrl+Shift+P and choose WPILib: Create a new project.

2

Choose Template, Java, Command Robot

The plain one, not the Skeleton: its comments are worth reading.

3

Set the folder, name and team number

Keep it out of OneDrive, then click Generate Project.

4

Install REVLib

Manage Vendor Libraries, then Install new libraries (online), then paste https://software-metadata.revrobotics.com/REVLib-2026.json

5

Build once

Run WPILib: Build Robot Code to prove the library is in.

6

Set up each SPARK in REV Hardware Client 2

Use 2026 firmware (26.x), then set the CAN ID and motor type.

REVLib install

docs.revrobotics.com: Installation

CANDriveSubsystem

Step 1: create the motors

CANDriveSubsystem.java

  // CIMs are BRUSHED motors: the classic KitBot bug.

2 private final SparkMax leftLeader =

1     new SparkMax(LEFT_LEADER_ID, MotorType.kBrushed);

2 private final SparkMax leftFollower =

1     new SparkMax(LEFT_FOLLOWER_ID, MotorType.kBrushed);

2 private final SparkMax rightLeader =

1     new SparkMax(RIGHT_LEADER_ID, MotorType.kBrushed);

2 private final SparkMax rightFollower =

1     new SparkMax(RIGHT_FOLLOWER_ID, MotorType.kBrushed);

   

3 private final DifferentialDrive drive =

3     new DifferentialDrive(leftLeader, rightLeader);

1

Brushed

CIMs have brushes. Tell the SPARK, because it can’t detect that.

2

Private

Only this class touches the motors.

3

Leaders only

DifferentialDrive gets one motor per side. Followers copy them.

Deck 2 · KitBot drive

6

CANDriveSubsystem

Step 2: build the config

CANDriveSubsystem.java

  SparkMaxConfig common = new SparkMaxConfig();

1 common.smartCurrentLimit(CURRENT_LIMIT_AMPS);

1 common.idleMode(IdleMode.kBrake);

   

  // Leaders only: followers copy their leader's output.

  SparkMaxConfig rightConfig = new SparkMaxConfig();

2 rightConfig.apply(common).voltageCompensation(NOMINAL_VOLTS);

  // One side must be inverted. On the KitBot, it's the left.

  SparkMaxConfig leftConfig = new SparkMaxConfig();

3 leftConfig.apply(rightConfig).inverted(true);

   

  SparkMaxConfig leftFollowerConfig = new SparkMaxConfig();

4 leftFollowerConfig.apply(common).follow(leftLeader);

  SparkMaxConfig rightFollowerConfig = new SparkMaxConfig();

4 rightFollowerConfig.apply(common).follow(rightLeader);

1

Shared by all four

The current limit and brake mode.

2

Leaders only

Voltage compensation. A follower mirrors the result, so it needs none.

3

One side inverted

The sides face opposite ways, and nothing flips one for you.

4

Followers

Each one mirrors its leader. Set nothing else on direction.

7

CANDriveSubsystem

Step 3: apply the config

CANDriveSubsystem.java

  // Reset: a swapped-in SPARK starts from a known state.

  // Persist: settings survive a brownout or breaker trip.

1 ResetMode reset = ResetMode.kResetSafeParameters;

2 PersistMode persist = PersistMode.kPersistParameters;

3 leftLeader.configure(leftConfig, reset, persist);

3 rightLeader.configure(rightConfig, reset, persist);

3 leftFollower.configure(leftFollowerConfig, reset, persist);

3 rightFollower.configure(rightFollowerConfig, reset, persist);

1

Reset

Starts from a known state, so a swapped-in spare behaves.

2

Persist

Saves to the SPARK, so settings survive a brownout or breaker trip.

3

Once, at startup

Saving takes time and blocks the SPARK. Never do it in a loop.

8

CANDriveSubsystem

Step 4: write the command factory

CANDriveSubsystem.java

/** Suppliers, not doubles: the stick is re-read on every 20 ms loop. */

public Command driveArcade(DoubleSupplier forward, DoubleSupplier rotation) {

  return run(() -> drive.arcadeDrive(forward.getAsDouble(), rotation.getAsDouble()))

      .withName("Arcade Drive");

}

run() makes a command that requires this subsystem. Suppliers let it re-read the stick on every loop.

Deck 2 · KitBot drive

9

RobotContainer

Step 5: bind the controller

RobotContainer.java

private void configureBindings() {

  // Sticks read negative when pushed away, and +rotation is counter-clockwise.

  drive.setDefaultCommand(

      drive.driveArcade(

          () -> -MathUtil.applyDeadband(driver.getLeftY(), DEADBAND) * DRIVE_SCALE,

          () -> -MathUtil.applyDeadband(driver.getRightX(), DEADBAND) * TURN_SCALE));

}

Minus signs: match the stick to the robot. Deadband: ignore a stick that rests slightly off zero. Scale: reduce the speed.

First test

First test: wheels off the ground

1

Prop the robot up

Wheels clear, hands clear. One person ready on Enter (disable). Space is E-stop.

2

Read the SPARK lights

Blue or yellow means brushed. Our code sets brake, so expect blue.

3

Check the controller

Driver Station USB Devices tab: slot 0, and the axes follow the sticks.

4

Enable Teleop and push forward gently

Both sides spin forward at the same speed.

5

Push the right stick right

Left wheels go forward, right wheels go back.

6

Let go, then check

Wheels stop. No red text in Messages. Nothing hot, and no bad smells.

11

Common mistake

CIMs set to kBrushless

What you see

The SPARK light shows magenta or cyan, the brushless colours, and may blink orange and magenta for a sensor fault.

Why it happens

A new SPARK ships set to brushless and can’t detect the motor. In that mode it looks for a motor sensor a CIM doesn’t have.

The fix

Use MotorType.kBrushed in code, and set the motor type to brushed in REV Hardware Client 2. Look for blue or yellow.

Deck 2 · KitBot drive

12

Common mistake

A CAN ID that does not match

What you see

The log shows [Spark Max] IDs: 6, Unable to retrieve SPARK firmware version and timed out while waiting. That motor stays still.

Why it happens

No SPARK answers at the ID in Constants. Every new SPARK ships as ID 0, and each needs its own number.

The fix

Set IDs in REV Hardware Client 2 over USB, robot off, one SPARK at a time. Then match Constants.

Common mistakes

Three more symptoms and what causes them

What you seeWhy it happensThe fix
Push forward and the robot spins on the spotNo side is inverted, so the two sides drive opposite waysAdd inverted(true) on one leader. The KitBot uses the left.
One side is weak, or motors run hot and a breaker tripsA follower is missing, follows the wrong leader, or is reversed, so two CIMs fight in one gearboxGive each follower .follow(itsLeader), with no true.
The left stick does nothing and the D-pad drivesThe F310 Mode light is on, or the back switch is on DSwitch to X, Mode light off, replug. Check the USB Devices tab.

14

Best practice

Never make the loop wait

No while loops or Thread.sleep in robot code.

Everything shares one 20 ms loop. If one command waits, every subsystem waits, and motor safety stops the drive.

// Wrong: the whole robot freezes for 2 seconds

Thread.sleep(2000);

 

// Right: the scheduler keeps looping while this runs

drive.driveArcade(() -> 0.5, () -> 0).withTimeout(2.0);

Deck 2 · KitBot drive

15

Sequences

One command that does three things in order

DriveAutos.java

/** Drive forward, hold still, then turn left: one command that does three things. */

public static Command forwardPauseTurn(CANDriveSubsystem drive) {

  return drive.driveArcade(() -> AUTO_SPEED, () -> 0.0).withTimeout(DRIVE_OUT_SECONDS)

      .andThen(drive.driveArcade(() -> 0.0, () -> 0.0).withTimeout(PAUSE_SECONDS))

      .andThen(drive.driveArcade(() -> 0.0, () -> AUTO_SPEED).withTimeout(TURN_SECONDS));

}

withTimeout ends each step. andThen starts the next step when the one before it ends.

Deck 2 · KitBot drive

16

Common mistake

A waitSeconds step in a drive sequence

What you see

During the pause, the Driver Station shows DifferentialDrive... Output not updated often enough.

Why it happens

Commands.waitSeconds runs no drive code, so nothing updates the drive. After 0.1 s, motor safety stops it and reports the error.

The fix

Hold the drive still with a step that drives at zero for the pause, as on the slide before.

// Error during the pause

forward.andThen(Commands.waitSeconds(1.0)).andThen(turn);

Sequences

Ways to combine commands

Write thisIt runsIt ends when
a.andThen(b)a, then bb ends
Commands.sequence(a, b, c)each one in orderthe last one ends
a.alongWith(b)a and b at the same timeboth have ended
a.raceWith(b)a and b at the same timeeither one ends
a.deadlineFor(b)a and b at the same timea ends, and b is cancelled
a.withTimeout(2.0)a for at most 2 secondsa ends or the time is up
a.until(condition)aa ends or the condition is true

18

Autonomous

An autonomous routine is one command

DriveAutos.java

/** The same routine as a list: easier to read, reorder and extend. */

public static Command leaveAndTurn(CANDriveSubsystem drive) {

  return Commands.sequence(

          drive.driveArcade(() -> AUTO_SPEED, () -> 0.0).withTimeout(DRIVE_OUT_SECONDS),

          drive.driveArcade(() -> 0.0, () -> 0.0).withTimeout(PAUSE_SECONDS),

          drive.driveArcade(() -> 0.0, () -> AUTO_SPEED).withTimeout(TURN_SECONDS),

          Commands.print("Auto finished"))

      .withName("Leave and turn");

}

getAutonomousCommand() in RobotContainer returns this. Robot.java runs it when autonomous starts and cancels it when teleop starts.

Deck 2 · KitBot drive

19

Best practice

Build a new command for each use

Call the factory again each time. One command object can go in only one group.

Reusing one makes WPILib throw: Commands that have been composed may not be added to another composition or scheduled individually!

// Wrong: one command object in two groups

Command fwd = drive.driveArcade(() -> 0.4, () -> 0.0).withTimeout(2.0);

Command autoA = Commands.sequence(fwd, Commands.print("A"));

Command autoB = Commands.sequence(fwd, Commands.print("B")); // throws

// Right: each call to the method makes a new command

Command autoC = DriveAutos.leaveAndTurn(drive);

Best practice

Five habits that keep robot code readable

HabitIn practiceWhy
Constants, not magic numbersLEFT_LEADER_ID, not 1Swap a motor and change one line
The subsystem owns its hardwareMotors are privateEvery use goes through the subsystem
Factories, not loose classesdrive.driveArcade(...)Less code, and the requirement is automatic
Name your commands.withName(“Arcade Drive”)Logs show a name you can read
Commit to git oftenCommit after each thing worksYou can always get back to working code

Exercise

Change the drive scale

1.

Set DRIVE_SCALE to 0.4 in Constants, deploy, and drive a slow lap.

2.

Set it back to 0.7, deploy, and drive the same lap.

3.

Commit your working code, with a message that says what it does.

Done when: both laps are driven, and your working code is committed.

Exercise

Run the timed autonomous

1.

Put the robot on blocks, wheels off the ground. Deploy.

2.

In Driver Station, choose Autonomous and enable. Watch the wheels.

3.

Set PAUSE_SECONDS to 2.0, deploy, and run it again.

Done when: the wheels drive forward, stop for two seconds, then turn, and the terminal prints Auto finished.
